engineChanges.entitlementMarker: GET feasibility-export status response gains `entitlement: {tier, granted, requiredTier, gatedSections}`, computed fresh from the CURRENT request's own gate-front context on every read -- no storage/schema change. This is not a new gap beyond the already-flagged, already-escalated Q5 direct-bypass hole.

falsifier: Pre-registered at CP1: 'If an unentitled live call returns a dollar or owner value from the engine after step 2, the gate is not in the path. If a missing header returns a value, the gate fails open. If the entitled path returns a refusal for the operator's own account, the tier mapping is wrong.' Observed, live, on both the canary tag and after the 100% traffic shift to production: a public-free-tier compose settles with parcelOwnership absent (kind entitlement-required) and entitlement.granted:false; a public-paid compose on a fresh parcel settles with entitlement.granted:true; a request with no gate-front headers at all still gets HTTP 401 before any route; this session's own live, authenticated Smart Site MCP connection received a real feasibility PDF for 48021:34049 (entitled account, production, post-deploy). None of the three falsifiers fired.
contradicted: P-152 lane 3's leave_behind and this dispatch's own 'What is true today' both stated 'smartsite-mcp has NO entitlement check before calling the engine.' False as stated for the only code path that reaches the engine: tools.ts's export_instrument handler already ran canRunStudioReport/hasPropertyUnlock before calling out. The real, narrower gap -- confirmed live via a read-only, pre-deploy GET against hauska-engine-api with hand-fabricated headers and no bearer token, which returned full job metadata for a real parcel -- was that the ENGINE itself enforced nothing server-side, making the MCP's local check necessary but not sufficient.

The dispatch's step-4 instrument named run_report and get_smart_site as the live-violation targets. Both call cortex-api's POST /api/property-explorer/v1/research/brief (legacy-design-tools), which reads LDT's own Postgres fact atoms directly under its own independent, pre-existing gate (requirePePaidOrPropertyUnlocked + grantsCadRollValuationFor) and never calls hauska-engine-api at all -- confirmed by reading propertyExplorer.ts and by the live MCP tool descriptions themselves (get_smart_site's own description states 'owner is a separate Studio/Team-gated read this tool does not carry at any depth'). Corrected to export_instrument kind:'feasibility' before any live testing; approved by the planner as Q6.

Step 4's suggested fallback 'the planner uses the anonymous path' does not exist for this connector: a raw, unauthenticated POST to smartsite-mcp's production /mcp endpoint returned {"error":"unauthorized","reason":"missing_bearer"} before reaching any tool or entitlement logic at all. Checked live rather than assumed.

missionPremise: The engine parses x-hauska-access-tier but no route or composer reads it to gate anything, and smartsite-mcp sends a static 'public-paid' header regardless of the caller -- an unentitled caller who could reach the engine at all would get the same dollar-rail and owner-info composition as an entitled one.
completionPredicate: A free-tier (or otherwise unentitled) live call to the gated composer refuses parcelOwnership with a typed reason; the identical entitled call composes real values; a missing gate-front header still fails closed; smartsite-mcp passes the caller's real resolved tier and surfaces the engine's own refusal, if one ever fires, in the same upgrade_required vocabulary the connector already publishes.
scopeBasis: Built, tested, merged, deployed, and live-verified in both directions on the deployed hauska-engine-api (canary and 100% production traffic) for the ONE composer confirmed to read dollar/owner data from the engine's own substrate; built, tested, merged and deployed on smartsite-mcp, with the entitled side of the full MCP round trip live-verified in production and the refused side verified by the equivalent live engine-direct test plus targeted unit tests, per the leave_behind above. Deliberately NOT touched: the unauthenticated-engine finding (Q5, escalated by the planner to the operator), the panel's own gating (P-152 lane 4, out of scope per the dispatch), pricing/tier definitions (P-119, authoritative), and hauska-mcp-server's siteplan/terrain/dossier proxy (a third repo, SUBSTRATE seat, outside this lane's two registered repos).
